objects_built.name: rate_limit
objects_built.role: Refuses a call when one client IP has made 10 or more calls to the same endpoint in the current minute; counts calls in rate_limit_hits

objects_built.name: rate_limit_hits
objects_built.role: One counter row per client IP, endpoint and one-minute window

objects_built.name: purge_rate_limit_hits
objects_built.role: Daily delete of counter rows whose window has ended

endpoints_need_login (AUTH-010): would require login on signup/login, which is wrong for a public signup
public_endpoints_harmless (AUTH-003): concerns writes from public endpoints, not rate limits

assumptions: $request.ip and $request.path are available in middleware and return the client address and endpoint path
precondition (false) with error_type accessdenied returns a refusal to the caller
a public endpoint is one with no auth line, or tagged public, per the workspace files; endpoint_auth none reflects Xano's own view and was not separately checked
enforcement advisory is the right default for a new policy; blocking left to the customer
confusions: The skill and catalogue say how to attach a middleware to an object only in prose ('attaching per object replaces inherited middleware'). They give no XanoScript example of the attachment statement itself, so I could not write it.
The Ask is for rate limiting, and the catalogue has no rate-limit check. I used object.middleware_required as the closest fit, which only proves attachment, not behaviour.
The AUTH-040 template's keywords include 'rate limit' but its rule requires login, so the keyword match is misleading for a public-endpoint rule.
The dry run reports 'Invalid block: name' and 'Invalid kind for middleware' errors without pointing at the valid form, which made the attachment syntax hard to find.
wished_for: A XanoScript example of attaching middleware to a single endpoint, with the phase setting
A rate-limit recipe or template (middleware plus counter table plus policy) for login and signup
A check or param that reads which endpoints run a given middleware in a given phase, so the rule's target is explicit
Documentation of the request-context variables available to middleware ($request.ip, path)
parse_errors_seen: Invalid block: name (on middleware = [{name: ..., phase: ...}] in query header)
Syntax error: unexpected 'middleware' (middleware rate_limit { phase = "pre" } block)
dry_run_problems_seen: Six endpoints blocked by middleware attachment syntax (all reverted); final dry run clean with the four new objects only
RATE-001.R1 warning from xano policy parse: rate_limit not on branch (expected before push)
why_confidence: The policy and the middleware are in place, but no public endpoint is attached to the middleware: the attachment syntax was rejected four times and I did not find the right form. Until the six endpoints are attached, the rule reports them and nothing is rate limited. Even after attachment, the counting logic and the request-context names are unverified, and the dry run does not check them.
